title: The Envelope
heading: BadCode Shorts ▲ The Envelope

beats.name: A. Approved (1)
beats.blurb: An arms-deal envelope lands on a desk, stamped APPROVED BY THE CONSERVATIVE PARTY.

beats.name: B. Approved (2)
beats.blurb: The next one lands: APPROVED BY THE LABOUR PARTY.

beats.name: C. Anyway
beats.blurb: "They're going to print the money and the weapon sales will still happen anyway, everything else is a distraction."

beats.name: S1. The set-up
beats.blurb: A 1930s backstreet 'betting parlour' where the race has two runners: the dealer fans two envelopes, APPROVED BY THE CONSERVATIVE PARTY and APPROVED BY THE LABOUR PARTY, at even odds.

beats.name: S2. The pick
beats.blurb: The working man, the mark, chooses one envelope in good faith; the dealer plays the fair host.

beats.name: S3. The switch
beats.blurb: Under the counter both envelopes are opened: the same arms order, same number, comes out of each, next to a drawer of freshly printed money. The choice was rigged both ways.

beats.name: S4. The sting
beats.blurb: BadCode rips back the curtain and catches the house: blue tie and red tie shaking hands over the stamped rifle crate and the new money. Spoken (and optionally on screen): "They're going to print the money and the weapon sales will still happen anyway, everything else is a distraction."

moodboard_intro: Round 3 (Jack's notes on round 2): column b, the painted chapter cards, is the look. S1 and S2 picked. S3 The Switch: "this style but more like the Sting": a sealed writer researched the film's cons (the wire, the bundle switch, the shell game) and staged three switches: a the dealer's hands (both envelopes hold the same order, a spare up his cuff), b the wire room (both envelopes strung to one telegraph key, shills in the doorway), c the shell game with bowler hats (same crate under both). S4 The Pay-off: "no skin for the badcode guy and fix the mask": mask fixed to the brand design, gauntlet gloves, the stray 'CHAPTER TITLE' gone. Note: the banknotes still look a bit like dollars; they get invented notes in the animation pass.
line: They're going to print the money and the weapon sales will still happen anyway, everything else is a distraction.
